title: Model Onboarding + Eval Harness + Quality Guardrails Playbook
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the combined process for onboarding new models into Redwood Inference, integrating them with the eval-harness, constructing prompt sets and benchmarks, defining quality guardrails, selecting quantization profiles, and running regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML, and platform engineers responsible for model serving readiness and ongoing quality monitoring.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable, auditable model onboarding flow that yields production-ready performance and predictable unit economics.
- Ensure models have comprehensive prompt sets, benchmarks, and guardrails before routing traffic.
- Minimize surprise regressions by standardizing evals and triage steps.

Scope:
- Applies to all open and internal models planned for Redwood-hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Includes model flavors (FP16, int8, quantized variants) and variants created during quantization/profile tuning.

Stakeholders and Ownership:
- Owner: Applied ML (owner_team: engineering) - primary contact for onboarding & evaluations.
- Runtime/Serving: Eng-serving-runtime - responsible for kernel selection and runtime integration.
- Platform/Observability: Eng-platform - responsible for dashboards, traces, and rollout automation hooks.
- Security/Compliance: Security-and-compliance - consent for restricted models or PII-sensitive benchmarks.

Prerequisites (before onboarding begins):
1) Model artifact uploaded to the model registry with semantic versioning (e.g., my-model:2026-01-15-1).
2) Baseline metadata populated: architecture, tokenizer, context window, FLOPs estimate, training data summary (high level).
3) Minimum viability test passing locally (tokenization roundtrip, basic forward pass smoke tests).

High-level Onboarding Checklist (step-by-step):
1. Create a new onboarding ticket (JIRA template: ML-ONBOARD) and attach the model artifact reference. Assign Applied ML owner and reviewers.
2. Add an entry in the model catalog (internal) with expected SLO targets and cost targets.
3. Register model with eval-harness and create an eval job definition (see Eval Harness Integration).
4. Author prompt sets for the model (see Prompt Sets and Benchmarks section).
5. Define quality guardrails and acceptance criteria (see Quality Guardrails).
6. Generate quantization profiles and validate the quantized variants (see Quantization Profiles).
7. Run the full benchmark suite and record results in the Benchmark Results table.
8. If regression detected, start Regression Triage (see Regression Triage Playbook).
9. Approve rollout strategy (canary %, regions, capacity tiers).
10. Schedule first production rollout and monitoring hooks.

Eval Harness Integration (how to wire model into the harness):
- Purpose: Standardize unit and end-to-end evaluation so that new models are compared against baseline models on the same metrics and datasets.
- Components: harness-runner (CLI), bench-def YAML, runner-config, result artifacts (JSON + compressed logs).
- Required fields in bench-def YAML:
  - name: short-name
  - model_ref: registry://<model>:<version>
  - datasets: [list of dataset ids]
  - metrics: [per-dataset metric list]
  - run_config: {batch_size, max_tokens, sampling_params}

Example bench-def (bench-def.yaml):
---
name: conversational-bench-v1
model_ref: registry://my-model:2026-01-15-1
datasets:
  - conv_safety_v2
  - conv_coherency_corpora
metrics:
  - exact_match
  - rouge_l
  - perplexity
run_config:
  batch_size: 16
  max_tokens: 256
  sampling_params:
    temperature: 0.0
    top_p: 0.95
---

CLI: run a full harness job locally or on CI
- Local dev: python -m harness.runner --def bench-def.yaml --out results.json --profile small
- CI/Cluster: harness submit --def bench-def.yaml --cluster large --notify slack:#ml-evals

Prompt Sets and Benchmarks (guidelines):
- Create prompt sets covering:
  - Core functional capabilities (task-specific prompts).
  - Edge cases & failure modes (long context, rare entities).
  - Safety-sensitive prompts (for safety/regulatory review).
  - Cost-sensitive synthetic workloads (to estimate tokens-per-response distribution).
- Each prompt set must include: id, short description, expected outputs, and an acceptance metric (e.g., >= 85% correctness on dataset X).
- Maintain a canonical mapping: prompt_set_id -> benchmark_suite_id for traceability.

Benchmark Results Table (template to include in model catalog entry):
| Metric | Dataset | Baseline Model | Candidate Model | Delta | Notes |
|--------|---------|----------------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| Rouge-L | conv_coherency_corpora | 42.1 | 44.8 | +2.7 | Improved long-context coherence |
| Safety-Block-rate | conv_safety_v2 | 0.8% | 1.1% | +0.3pp | Needs review from safety |

Quality Guardrails (acceptance criteria and automated checks):
- Types of guardrails:
  - Quality thresholds (task metrics, e.g., rouge, exact match).
  - Safety thresholds (unsafe content classification rates).
  - Latency & throughput SLOs (p90, p99).
  - Cost targets (tokens per response, batch efficiency).
- Default acceptance thresholds for Hosted evaluation:
  - Task-quality: candidate must be within +/-1.5% absolute of baseline on key metrics or better.
  - Safety: unsafe content rate <= baseline + 0.2pp and absolute <= 1.5%.
  - Latency: p95 <= 1.5x baseline runtime for same hardware/profile.
  - Cost: tokens-per-response median within 10% of baseline.
- If any threshold fails, model status = "blocked" and Regression Triage must be started.

Quantization Profiles (profile creation and validation):
- Goal: reduce token compute cost while maintaining acceptable quality.
- Profiles must be authored as top-level YAML files and checked into the model directory. Fields (example):
  - profile_name: int8-default
  - quant_backend: qdrp-v2
  - per_channel: true
  - excluded_layers: [layer_norm, output_head]
  - calibration_dataset: quant_calib_small_v1
  - validation_metrics: [rouge_l, perplexity, safety_block_rate]

Example quant profile (quant-profile.yaml):
---
profile_name: int8-default
quant_backend: qdrp-v2
per_channel: true
excluded_layers:
  - layer_norm
  - lm_head
calibration_dataset: quant_calib_small_v1
validation_metrics:
  - rouge_l
  - perplexity
  - safety_block_rate
---

Validation steps for quantized variants:
1) Run calibration on the declared dataset.
2) Run the same eval-harness bench-def but with model_ref pointing to the quantized artifact.
3) Compare metrics against FP16 baseline using the Benchmark Results Table template.
4) If quality regressions exceed guardrail thresholds, custom tuning is required (per-channel vs per-tensor, exclude layers).

Regression Triage Playbook (when a regression is detected):
1. Triage kickoff: open a triage ticket (TAG: REGRESS) and set severity based on customer impact.
2. Gather artifacts: failing examples, eval job logs, perf traces, model metadata, quant profiles run. Attach to ticket.
3. Quick classification (within 4 hours):
   - Class A: deterministic model change (e.g., weights changed, prompt tune applied).
   - Class B: environment/regression (runtime, kernel change).
   - Class C: data drift/metric noise (dataset differences).
4. If Class A: revert to last-known-good model and pin rollout; create PR to block the offending change.
5. If Class B: involve eng-serving-runtime for kernel/config rollback and investigate hardware/drivers.
6. If Class C: expand dataset and re-evaluate; consider adjusting acceptance thresholds or adding new prompts.
7. For quantization-specific regressions: run a per-layer sensitivity analysis (script: tools/quant/sensitivity_scan.py --model <artifact> --out sensitivity.json).
8. Decision: fix-tune-model / adjust-quant-profile / rollback. Record action and owner in ticket.
9. Postmortem: for severity >= P2, schedule a 2-week retrospective and publish a short incident summary in confluence (link back to ticket).

Rollout and Monitoring (post-approval):
- Recommended rollout: canary 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 24-48 hour observation windows unless low-risk.
- Monitoring hooks required before canary: per-route latency p50/p95/p99, token-cost breakdown, key metric deltas, safety block rate.
- Automatic rollback triggers (examples):
  - task-quality drop > 2.0% absolute on primary metric for > 10m window.
  - safety_block_rate increase > 0.5pp sustained for > 10m.
  - latency p99 increase > 2.0x baseline for > 5m.

Templates and Artifacts (where to store):
- Model catalog entry: /models/<model-name>/<version>/catalog.json (metadata + links to results).
- Bench-defs and quant profiles: store under model repo: models/<model-name>/eval/bench-def.yaml and models/<model-name>/quant/quant-profile.yaml.
- Eval artifacts (results.json, logs): store in eval-archive bucket: s3://redwood-eval-archive/<model>/<run-id>/

Common Tools and Commands:
- Run full eval locally: python -m harness.runner --def models/my-model/eval/bench-def.yaml --out /tmp/results.json
- Submit to cluster: harness submit --def models/my-model/eval/bench-def.yaml --cluster eval-large --notify slack:#ml-evals
- Quick quant sensitivity scan: python tools/quant/sensitivity_scan.py --model registry://my-model:2026-01-15-1 --out /tmp/sens.json

Operational SLOs and Reporting:
- Evaluation coverage: 100% of new models must complete the eval-harness suite before approval.
- Time-to-onboard target: median 3 business days from ticket open to first eval results for minor models, 10 business days for large models requiring quantization tuning.
- Regression response: initial triage within 4 hours, mitigation plan within 24 hours for P1/P2 regressions.

Appendix A: Acceptance Checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Model artifact registered and metadata complete
- [ ] Bench-def created and linked to ticket
- [ ] Prompt sets authored and validated
- [ ] Benchmarks run, results recorded in table
- [ ] Quant profiles added (if applicable) and validated
- [ ] Guardrails satisfied or exceptions documented
- [ ] Rollout plan documented (canary percentages, regions)
- [ ] Monitoring dashboard and alerting configured
